DeployBot: Automated hold: Canary for release v2.14.1 paused due to incident INC-2026 (EU ingress 503 spike). All subsequent slots are on hold. /deploy status: CANARY_PAUSED :warning:
harper: saw the alert, thanks. Is this the new ingress surge we saw earlier?
jenna: yep, same cluster. I'm on it with SRE. label: urgent
leo: recommend we don't roll back yet — can we hold and pin the current image at v2.14.0 for other lanes?
maddy: @leo +1 for pinning non-canary lanes. If canary is flapping, we avoid cascading.
sre-oncall-bot: Oncall engaged: @maddy @jenna. Looking at 503s from proxy -> k8s svc. Investigating backend pool health.
jenna: quick ask — can someone update changelog/release notes to mark the canary paused and planned hotpatch? avoids confusion for product team.
harper: I'll add a short note to the release page: "Canary paused due to EU ingress errors; hotpatch planned; do not proceed with downstream slots."
kevin: ops question — if we pin, what's the command?
leo: run `./deploy pin --env=prod --version=2.14.0 --reason="canary pause INC-2026"` or use the Console -> Releases -> Pin version.
jenna: if SRE can confirm root cause within 30m, we can resume canary. If not, hotpatch is safer. Thoughts on rollback vs hotpatch?
maddy: rollback risks regressing changes in telemetry fixes. Hotpatch targeted fix faster usually. I'm leaning hotpatch.
sre-oncall-bot: root cause: upstream LB config propagation delay + one unhealthy backend causing TCP resets. Mitigation: remove unhealthy backend + redeploy proxy config. ETA ~25m.
harper: given that, do we want to proceed with hotpatch window at +45m? I can move the change window and notify stakeholders.
leo: yes schedule hotpatch window +45m. Meanwhile pin other lanes. I'll execute the pin now.
DeployBot: Action: `pin` executed by leo at 6161239990. Result: production lanes pinned to v2.14.0.
kevin: thanks. I'll update internal release notes: add a block under "Status" -> "Canary paused; hotpatch scheduled; other lanes pinned."
jenna: SRE, once proxy config rolled back/removed unhealthy node, can we do a smoke test in EU before resuming canary?
sre-oncall-bot: will run smoke test after removal and post results here.
maddy: add a canary resume checklist in the release doc so QA knows to re-run prompt-set A and latency checks.
harper: done — checklist added and I pinged product slack.
DeployBot: Scheduled hotpatch window for v2.14.1 at 6161242600 (in ~45m). Canary resume tentatively at 6161244200 after validation.
leo: final question — do we tag the hotpatch as v2.14.1-hotfix1 and include in release notes?
jenna: yes. I'll cut hotfix branch after SRE confirms root cause gone and include rollback instructions in notes.
kevin: pinging security to verify no data exposure.
sre-oncall-bot: smoke test passed at 6161243150: 503 rate back to baseline. Ready for hotpatch and canary resume.
maddy: proceeding with hotpatch plan. @harper please coordinate release note header: "Hotfix scheduled; canary paused/resumed timeline"
harper: on it. I will also create a short internal postmortem stub referencing INC-2026.
leo: thanks team. once hotpatch merged, let's run a staged canary at 10% then 50% then full. use the rollout policy `stair-step-10-50-100`.
DeployBot: Hotpatch merge queued. Closing note: deploys remain on hold until hotpatch completes and staged canary passes.
harper: closing this thread when hotpatch completes. cc: @product @support for downstream comms. :white_check_mark:
